89:     \label{forumle23}
90:     \begin{split}

93:     \end{split}
94:     \end{align}

96:     \begin{enumerate}
97:         \item \((x_1+x_2)l = x_1l + x_2l, \qquad x(l_1 + l_2) = xl_1 + xl_2,\)
98:         \item\(\alpha (xl) = (\alpha x)l = x(\alpha l)\)
99:         \item\(x[l_1l_2] = (xl_1)l_2 - (xl_2)l_1\)
100:     \end{enumerate}
101:     We shall now use these conditions to define the concept of an
102:     $\frL$-module, $\frL$ a Lie algebra. This is a vector space $\frM$ over $\Phi$ with a mapping of $\frM \times \frL$ to $\frM$ such that the result $xl$ satisfies 1, 2,
103:     and 3 above.
